original_summary: Melos, a shepherd, is arrested in a city ruled by a tyrant who kills people based only on suspicion. The ruler sentences Melos to death, but allows him three days to return home for his sister’s wedding while his friend remains as a hostage. On his journey back, Melos faces a flooded river, bandits, and terrible exhaustion, and he nearly gives up before renewing his promise and trust. He reaches the city just before the execution, saving his friend and moving the ruler to change.
seed_elements: A shepherd named Melos openly denounces a tyrant who executes suspected enemies without fair trials.
Melos is sentenced to death but receives three days to attend his sister’s wedding, with his friend held hostage in his place.
Melos must race back to the city before the execution begins.
A series of obstacles, including dangerous water and attackers, delays and weakens him.
At his lowest point, Melos is tempted to give up and let his friend die, but he revives and recommits to his promise through trust.
Melos arrives just in time; his friend is freed, and the ruler is changed by their loyalty and mutual trust.
discarded_elements: Personal names for the friend, the ruler, the sister, or other minor characters
Minor wedding details and extra family or city subplots
The exact number and full description of the river and bandit episodes
Excess historical, legendary, or technical detail
Long speeches and repeated reflections that are difficult for A2 readers
conversion_plan: Keep the kingdom and tyrant setting because the execution gives the promise its serious stakes; do not modernize the event. Write it mainly in simple third-person English at about 300–350 words, using only Melos as a personal name and role descriptions such as “his friend” and “the ruler” for the others. Preserve the obstacle sequence, Melos’s near-collapse and temptation to abandon his friend, his renewed resolve, and his last-minute arrival while simplifying the language and minor details for A2 learners.
